A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hybrid Policy Distillation for LLMs by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning, dialogue, and coding experiments, component ablations, and subsequent OPD/DPO training results in Sections 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds efficiency comparisons, stronger-teacher distillation results, and a training–benchmark overlap analysis.

M1.justification: The HPD objective, token weights, masking and reinforcement rules, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new emphasis on prefilling-time sampling explains the existing procedure; it does not establish an algorithm modification.

E1.justification: The reported HPD training and performance-evaluation datasets remain unchanged. Appendix J.2 adds Minerva to the datasets examined for training–benchmark overlap, a limited extension of audit coverage; no Minerva model-performance results are reported. The new Qwen3 models and generation caps are configuration changes.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 adds actual efficiency and coding comparisons against AKL and ABKD, which v1 discussed only as related work. This substantially strengthens comparisons with competing divergence-based distillation methods. The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a resource-comparison protocol using batch size 32, 10,240-token sequences, bfloat16 logits, and memory/time measures. It also adds Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 to Qwen3-0.6B distillation with a 20K training bound and 20K/38K evaluation caps. These substantially extend experimental settings without revising the retained Section 5 protocols.

E4.justification: New Section 7 examines computational tradeoffs, a larger teacher–student gap, and sensitivity to generation length. Appendix J.2 adds an exact/near-duplicate contamination audit. These substantially broaden supplementary validation; the original component ablations and Appendix K case study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix J.3 and Table 14 newly report 95% confidence intervals for six Arena-Hard entries. Existing reasoning-result averaging and t-tests remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish additional runs, and v2 does not explain how the new intervals were constructed.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and DPO results are retained unchanged, but v2 adds substantial resource, comparator, stronger-teacher, and overlap results. For example, Table 6 reports coding training times of 7h30m for HPD, 27h for AKL, and 14h for ABKD; Table 7 reports original-to-HPD AIME-24 scores of 11.35 to 15.78 at 38K. Table 13 adds overlap counts. New Table 14 lists Base Arena-Hard as 7.47, inconsistent with 9.90 in retained Table 3; this is not an established performance change.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, definitions, assumptions, and gradient derivations in Sections 2–4 and Appendices B–D are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified reweighted-likelihood perspective and efficient HPD with improved distillation and subsequent-training performance. The revised contribution bullet and conclusion describe the existing token-level mechanism more explicitly; the new experiments support retained claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly attributes resource savings to two-token operations, one teacher forward pass, and prefilling-time sampling, and interprets the larger-gap results as evidence of scaling. The same-tokenizer limitation, initialization positioning, and existing result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds vocabulary size, numerical precision, resource-accounting settings, training times, and explicit prefilling/teacher-pass descriptions. Appendix J.2 documents normalization, 6-gram candidate generation, SequenceMatcher, and manual auditing. Existing hyperparameter tables and code-access information are retained; profiling hardware and final overlap-audit decisions remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and dedicated Related Work discussion are substantively unchanged. New Section 7 sharpens HPD's positioning against already-cited AKL and ABKD through efficiency comparisons and contrasts its response lengths with prior KD settings.

P1.justification: v2 inserts an In-Depth Analysis section and Appendices J.2–J.3, rewrites one contribution bullet and the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements and publication/author-note updates. Most existing prose and the document's organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for efficiency, stronger-teacher results, overlap counts, and confidence intervals. Existing tables and Figure 4 shift with pagination, and case-study boxes reflow. The original figures are unchanged, and the overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides quantitative support for the efficiency claim, evaluates relevant additional comparators, and tests a larger teacher–student gap. The overlap audit and confidence intervals also improve transparency. These benefits are limited by missing profiling details, unreported overlap-audit outcomes, and Table 14's Base-score inconsistency with Table 3. The additions strengthen the evidence without establishing a substantial overall quality improvement.
